chunks: He said: For every two hundred dirhams, five dirhams [are due] from silver; and if it falls short, there is no zakat upon you.
And from gold, for every twenty dinars, half a dinar; and if it falls short, there is nothing upon you.

key_terms.الذهب: al-Dhahab: gold; zakat on gold parallels that on silver with the same 2.5% rate
key_terms.الفضة: al-Fidda: silver; zakat on silver is one of the original eight categories of zakatable wealth
key_terms.زكاة: Zakat: the obligatory alms-tax, one of the pillars of Islam, due on specified categories of wealth
key_terms.نِصَاب: Nisab: minimum threshold of wealth below which zakat is not obligatory

ai.seo_question: What is the nisab and rate of zakat on silver and gold according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) sets out the nisab (minimum threshold) and rate for zakat on silver and gold. For silver, the nisab is 200 dirhams with a 2.5% rate (5 dirhams per 200); for gold, the nisab is 20 dinars with the same 2.5% rate (half a dinar per 20). If one's holdings fall below the nisab, no zakat is owed. This ruling was transmitted through Sama'a, a prominent companion who collected many fiqh narrations from the Imam.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘With regards to every two hundred Dirhams there are five Dirhams from silver, and if it is deficient, so there is no Zakāt upon you;
and from the gold, from every twenty Dinars, half a Dinar, and if it is deficient, so there is nothing upon you’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘On every two hundred dirham of silver Zakat is five dirham, and on less than two hundred Zakat is not due.
On every twenty Dinar of gold half dinar is Zakat and on less than this Zakat is not due.’”
